text: An isolated incident cannot usually amount to a private nuisance.
Describe the elements of the tort of private nuisance and assess the validity of the statement
above. [25]
Describe the rules governing nervous shock and assess the fairness of these rules in relation to
rescuers and bystanders. [25]
Trespass to the person seeks to protect the individual from unlawful interference with their bodily
integrity.
Describe the legal rules governing trespass to the person and assess the validity of the statement
above. [25]
Section B
Malik and Naseem are in the same law class in college. Malik has recently passed his driving test
and has a driving licence. Naseem is still learning to drive and does not have a driving licence.
Malik drives to college and Naseem travels with him in the car. One day Naseem asks if he can
drive as he is taking his driving test soon and would like to practise. Malik agrees on condition that
Naseem drives along a less busy route and avoids the main roads.
After driving around the quiet roads, Naseem tells Malik that he is going to join a main road as he
needs to practise on a road with more traffic. Malik asks him not to do so but Naseem continues
on. When joining the main road Naseem fails to check for other vehicles and collides with another
car. Malik and Naseem both sustain serious injuries. The driver of the other car, Oliver, sustains a
broken leg and his car is completely destroyed.
Advise the parties as to their rights, responsibilities and remedies in negligence. [25]
Jade owns a large farm outside Barchester. A line of tall trees on Jade’s land marks the boundary
between her farm and a public road. During a storm one of the trees falls on to the road, landing
on Kevin’s car and causing significant damage.
The other side of Jade’s farm shares a fenced boundary with land owned by Liam. He has recently
started keeping horses. One of the horses leans over the fence and eats from a plant growing on
Jade’s land. The leaves of this plant are poisonous and the horse subsequently dies.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in relation to the rule in Rylands v Fletcher.
Padma has an appointment to see a doctor at ABC Health Clinic. She drives to the clinic and finds
the visitor car park. She sees a sign displaying the price for parking and is shocked to see how
expensive it is. She drives around the car park and sees a section which is clearly signposted as
‘Free Parking for Staff Only’. She parks in this section of the car park and is pleased that she does
not have to pay.
As Padma is now late for her appointment she decides not to walk back to the pedestrian crossing
to the clinic but instead walks directly towards the building up a steep muddy hill. She slips on the
way up the hill and falls. She sustains a broken arm and breaks her expensive spectacles.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in relation to occupier’s liability. [25]
